question.problem: Suppose $\mathbf a=[6,\, -3,\, 2]^T,$ and $\mathbf b=[7,\, -1,\, 1]^T,$ and $p=4.$ Find the Minkowski distance $d_p$ between $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the Minkowski distance is defined as

$$
d_p(\mathbf a,\mathbf b) =\|\mathbf a-\mathbf b\|_p
$$

where for an $N$-dimensional vector $\mathbf v,$

$$
\|\mathbf v\|_p = \left(\sum_{i=1}^N |v_i|^p \right)^{1/p}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}_{4}(a,b) & =‖a-b{‖}_{4} \\  & ={‖[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]‖}_{4} \\  & ={(|6-7{|}^{4}+|-3-(-1){|}^{4}+|2-1{|}^{4})}^{1/4} \\  & ={18}^{1/4} \\  & ≈2.060,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
